decisions.statement: A registration names a link outside every checkout rather than a path inside one.
The link's own path is the one thing a running client holds that never changes.
A link is named for the event the client calls that link at.
Every link points at the one dispatch the index answers for.
The dispatch is reached through the index rather than spelled here.
A link already pointing where it should is left alone.
A link pointing into another checkout at a file that is there is left alone.
A link pointing at a file that is gone is written again by a run in the checkout the links serve.
A tree mounted for one run is another checkout, so a run there claims no link.
A link is put in place by a rename, so no call finds the path holding nothing.
The links sit under a folder outliving a reboot rather than under a run folder.
The events a mend covers are the names the links folder already holds.
A mend reads the index only where some link points at a file that is gone.
A mend that fails answers what failed rather than stopping its caller.
The name that answer opens with is handed in rather than spelled here.
A name carrying the mark of a half-written link is no event.
The dispatch cannot write the link a client reaches the dispatch through.
Nothing here reads a hook or judges a call.
Only a run in the checkout the links serve claims a link.
The checkout the links serve is the one the environment names.
A tree mounted for one run is known by the mount the environment names.
The environment names that mount and that checkout as one path under the mount.
A root that cannot be matched against that checkout claims no link.

definition: the fixed path outside the repository a hook is registered through
